policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: ASV opens the verse with 'For I would not, brethren, have you ignorant', a causal connective rendering γάρ; δέ would give 'Now/But'.
'were all baptized unto Moses' renders either the middle ἐβαπτίσαντο or the passive ἐβαπτίσθησαν; ASV uses the English passive for both voices here and no note distinguishes them.
Pure transposition of adjective and noun; 'the same spiritual food' is the only English order available for either sequence.
Transposition only; 'did all drink the same spiritual drink' renders either order. The verse's sole note is an alternative_rendering about 'the Christ' and cannot decide a reading.
Word order of the postpositive δέ with πέτρα; 'and the rock was Christ' is the same English either way.
ASV text reads 'make trial of the Lord' (κύριον), and the mapped textual_variant note 'Some ancient authorities read Christ' places Χριστόν in the margin, not the text.
'as some of them made trial' renders καθώς; the added adverbial καί ('even as') is routinely left unrendered by ASV, so the English does not exclude it.
'and perished' renders imperfect ἀπώλλυντο or aorist ἀπώλοντο alike; the note about Christ bears on v006 only.
καθάπερ and καθὼς καί are both rendered simply 'as some of them murmured'; nothing in the English separates them.
ASV reads 'Now these things happened unto them', with no 'all'; the added πάντα would be rendered, as ASV renders πάντα elsewhere in this chapter ('All things are lawful').
ASV renders an adverb, 'happened unto them by way of example', with the mapped gloss 'Greek by way of figure'; the plural predicate noun τύποι would give 'happened unto them as figures/ensamples'.
'the ends of the ages are come' fits perfect κατήντηκεν and is also ASV's ordinary rendering of an aorist here; no note distinguishes the tenses.
'that ye may be able to endure it' supplies the subject English requires for the infinitive, so it neither shows nor excludes an explicit ὑμᾶς.
Transposition of the copula within the clause; 'is it not a communion of the blood of Christ?' is fixed English word order either way. Both notes are alternative_rendering.
οὐχ and οὐχί are orthographic variants of the same negative; 'have not they that eat' renders both.

ASV's order 'that a thing sacrificed to idols is anything, or that an idol is anything' matches εἰδωλόθυτόν first and excludes RP's reversed r02; between r00 and r01 the only difference is an explicit ἐστιν, which English must supply in any case.

ASV names the subject, 'the things which the Gentiles sacrifice', so τὰ ἔθνη stands in the text and r00 is excluded; the remaining difference is verb number with a neuter plural subject, which English 'the Gentiles sacrifice' cannot show.
'they sacrifice to demons, and not to God' fixes the English order regardless of whether θύουσιν follows or precedes καὶ οὐ θεῷ.
ASV reads 'All things are lawful' without 'for me'; the added μοι would be rendered by a dative of reference ASV does not have.
The second clause likewise reads 'All things are lawful' with no 'for me', so the added μοι is absent from the text ASV rendered.
ASV reads 'but each his neighbor's good': 'each' renders ἕκαστος, which the base text lacks, and it is not marked as an italicized supply.
Order of postpositive γάρ with κυρίου only; 'for the earth is the Lord's' is the same English for both.
ASV begins 'If one of them that believe not biddeth you' with no connective, but it frequently leaves a transitional δέ unrendered, so the English does not exclude it.
ASV reads 'This hath been offered in sacrifice' with no reference to idols, rendering ἱερόθυτον; εἰδωλόθυτον is rendered 'a thing sacrificed to idols' at v. 19.
ASV ends the verse at 'for conscience' sake'; the added clause 'for the earth is the Lord's, and the fulness thereof' appears only at v. 26 and is absent here.
Transposition of the imperative with καὶ Ἰουδαίοις; 'Give no occasion of stumbling, either to Jews' renders either order.
σύμφορον and συμφέρον are alternative forms of the same idea, both rendered 'profit'.
